headline: 16-story building with 196 residential units and 330-space garage approved at 99 Lowell Street
summary: The project includes up to 7,325 square feet of commercial space on the first level and a three-story parking garage on the existing municipal parking lot. The applicant is Fusin O'Neill for the city of Manchester, and the approval added a condition on Pine Street curb line adjustments. Other approvals include a parking reduction at 223 Second Street, a subdivision at 659 Montgomery Street, and one added unit at 502 Cartier Street.
decisions: Approved waivers for driveway dimensions and general lighting at 99 Lowell Street.
Approved adding curb line adjustments to the Pine Street parking condition for 99 Lowell Street.
Approved site plan for 99 Lowell Street with all recommendations, including the amended condition nine.
Approved conditional use permit for a parking reduction at 223 Second Street.
Approved adding a granite curbing condition along the frontage at 659 Montgomery Street.
Approved subdivision at 659 Montgomery Street, creating one new buildable lot.
Approved five waivers for the site plan at 502 Cartier Street.
Approved site plan to add one dwelling unit at 502 Cartier Street.
Found three new applications do not have regional impact and do not warrant regional review.
discussion: Off-site parking access: Public comment raised concerns about reaching the churches and cathedral from the Victory Garage. Members said the off-site path would be rebuilt to ADA standards and the Chestnut Street crossing shortened.

Parking count at 99 Lowell Street: The 330 vehicle spaces exceed the zero required in the DT2 district, and members called the count reasonable for the planned units. The count does not include an additional 25 spaces in the commercial area.

Building design and shadows: Members said the brick appears high quality and that the renderings showed nothing they would change. The shadow study showed the building avoiding the nearby church and cathedral except in the darkest months.

223 Second Street parking reduction: Testimony said many visitors do not own cars, and the existing lot would get an updated sign and at least one bike rack. The site is on a bus line, and a paved rail trail is nearby.
Four-unit review threshold: Members discussed raising the four-unit review threshold to five or six units. Members could talk with staff about whether that change makes sense.
